key_patterns: THEMES-vs-SKINS are separate axes. A `data-theme` on <html> sets CSS custom properties (colors) in src/app.css; a 'skin' (layout components under src/lib/skins/{premium,classic,slate,aurora,festival}) is chosen by the pure map src/lib/skins/skinMap.ts (THEME_SKIN_ID). festival-dark and heritage-serif-dark BOTH map to the 'festival' skin. The no-flash script in src/app.html and src/lib/stores/theme.ts BOTH set data-theme AND toggle the `dark` class for dark themes (both ids ARE already in app.html's DARK map). The festival skin's cards use OPAQUE token backgrounds: src/lib/skins/festival/fest.ts CARD = 'bg-[rgb(var(--surface-bg))] ...' and text color 'text-[rgb(var(--fest-ink))]'. Other skins (slate/aurora/premium) use the .surface CSS class (translucent white via var(--surface-bg)/var(--surface-alpha)) over a dark page canvas, plus Tailwind dark: variants.
root_cause: PURE CSS SPECIFICITY BUG in src/app.css. The generic dark rule `:root.dark { --surface-bg: 255 255 255; --surface-alpha: 0.06; }` has specificity (0,2,0). The two festival-skin dark themes declare their intended DARK opaque surface with a plain attribute selector `[data-theme='festival-dark'] { --surface-bg: 42 20 24; }` and `[data-theme='heritage-serif-dark'] { --surface-bg: 26 32 29; }` at specificity (0,1,0). Because both `data-theme='festival-dark'` AND class `dark` are present on <html> together, `:root.dark` (0,2,0) OVERRIDES the theme block, so --surface-bg resolves to WHITE (255 255 255). The festival CARD paints an OPAQUE white background from that token, while --fest-ink stays a light cream (255 236 214 / 231 229 228) -> light/cream text on a white card = unreadable. VERIFIED empirically in a real browser: getComputedStyle(--surface-bg) returns '255 255 255' for both ids when .dark is set. Other dark themes (slate-dark, aurora, midnight) also get --surface-bg overridden to white@0.06 by :root.dark, but that is HARMLESS/intended for them because their skins use .surface (translucent) over a dark page and never paint an opaque surface from that token. So ONLY the two festival-skin dark themes break.
chosen_fix: Lowest-risk, CSS-only: raise the specificity of ONLY the two festival-skin dark theme blocks so their --surface-bg (and the other tokens they set) win over :root.dark. Change the two selectors in src/app.css from `[data-theme='festival-dark']` to `:root[data-theme='festival-dark']` and `[data-theme='heritage-serif-dark']` to `:root[data-theme='heritage-serif-dark']`. That yields specificity (0,2,0), tying :root.dark, and because these blocks appear LATER in source order they win. VERIFIED in a real browser: after the change getComputedStyle(--surface-bg) returns '42 20 24' and '26 32 29' respectively (dark) while --fest-ink stays cream -> dark card + light text = readable, WCAG-adequate. Do NOT change slate-dark/aurora/midnight/other themes (they must keep :root.dark's translucent surface). Do NOT alter the heritage-serif h1/h2/h3 serif rule or any other block. This adds ZERO JS bytes.
